title: Article 265: Can Government Levy Taxes Without a Law?
description: Article 265 of the Indian Constitution mandates that no tax can be imposed or collected by the government without a valid law. This constitutional provision a.

faq.q: What is Article 265 of the Indian Constitution?
faq.a: Article 265 states that "No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law." It means that every tax imposed by the government must be backed by a valid law passed by Parliament or a State Legislature.

faq.q: Can the government impose a new tax without passing a law?
faq.a: No, the government cannot impose a new tax without passing a specific law for it. Any new tax must go through the legislative process and be enacted into law by the Parliament or a State Legislature.

faq.q: What is the difference between a tax and a fee in the context of Article 265?
faq.a: Article 265 specifically applies to taxes. While a tax is a compulsory exaction for public purposes without a direct quid pro quo, a fee is generally charged for specific services rendered by the government. Fees are not strictly covered by Article 265 but must also have statutory backing.

faq.q: Who is responsible for making tax laws in India?
faq.a: Tax laws in India are made by the Parliament for central taxes (like Income Tax, Central GST) and by the respective State Legislatures for state taxes (like State GST, Stamp Duty).

faq.q: What recourse do citizens have if a tax is imposed without proper legal authority?
faq.a: If a tax is imposed without the authority of law, citizens can challenge it in a court of law, typically through a writ petition in a High Court or the Supreme Court, citing the violation of Article 265.
